name: Ashvale Pressed Occasion Jacket
description:
A single-button jacket in dark navy synth-polyester blend, originally manufactured as part of a Tier 2 office uniform line and now circulating through resale markets in significant volume. The construction is utilitarian — fused interfacing rather than stitched, a single internal pocket, and shoulder seams that sit slightly wide on most frames. The lining is a slick beige acetate that catches static. Despite its origins, the jacket reads as intentionally formal from a distance, which is the point.

At Φ22, this is the most common 'occasion jacket' on the Shelf and lower Tier 2. It appears at everything from corponation subsidiary job fairs to Ouroboros insurance dispute mediations to community hall weddings. Augment-incompatible by design, though many owners have cut their own port-access slits into the back panel and hemmed the edges with iron-on tape.
cultural_context: Recognized by anyone who grew up on the Shelf as 'the hearing jacket' or 'the interview jacket' — there's only a few styles that circulate at this price point and everyone knows them. Wearing one signals you're doing your best with what you have. Some Tier 3 people feel vague discomfort when they see it; they wore the same jacket once.
story_hooks: A synthetic being attending their personhood classification hearing has been advised by their advocate to wear something that reads as 'human formal' — this jacket is what they could afford.
Two strangers at a Tier 2 job fair recognize each other's identical jackets and share a moment of wordless solidarity before the recruiter calls the first name.
A Tier 4 corponation HR rep pulls a candidate's jacket subtly to check the label during a handshake — and what she does with that information defines her character.
